source.title: Decomposing Representation Space into Interpretable Subspaces with Unsupervised Learning

record.tranche_reason: The study uses the previously described GPT-2 IOI circuit to define an evaluation suite for its subspace method. Its results measure concentration of circuit-related target information across subspaces, not whether the IOI head circuit or its claimed roles hold.
record.gate_note: The paper patches residual-stream subspaces at locations selected from the known IOI circuit and reports Gini coefficients for the resulting effects. It does not ablate or patch the 26 attention heads, test the circuit’s faithfulness/completeness/minimality, or report IOI accuracy after removing everything outside the circuit. The IOI prompts vary name order and template, but results are aggregated rather than comparing prompt variants. Rows below record the reported IOI-related concentration results as findings outside the listed claim versions.
record.test_reason: The paper takes the Wang et al. IOI circuit as ground truth to choose patching sites (h4 at S1+1/IO+1, h6 at S2, h8 at END) and target information. It reports only how concentrated its NDM subspace patching effects are (Gini coefficients) against other partition baselines. It never ablates or patches the circuit's heads, tests faithfulness, completeness or minimality, ablates name movers, compares circuit-finding methods, or compares prompt variants. Its results evaluate the subspace method, not the circuit.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that NDM finds interpretable, consistent subspaces whose patching effects concentrate the target information of known GPT-2 circuits. They also conclude it scales to 2B models via separate context and parametric knowledge subspaces. They treat the IOI circuit as established ground truth and do not test it.
record.recipe_differences: Uses unsupervised neighbor-distance minimization to decompose residual-stream activations, then patches subspaces and measures concentration; the original IOI work identifies and tests a head-level causal circuit. This paper uses the original circuit to define its evaluation locations and target information.
record.method_sensitivity: For the paper’s subspace-concentration evaluation, GPT-2 results vary with NDM search number, merging interval and threshold (Table 5); OpenWebText yields worse aggregate results than MiniPile, with the authors saying tests 2–5 are affected (Table 7). Cosine distance gives similar or slightly worse aggregate results than Euclidean distance (Table 6). These are sensitivities of the subspace-method evaluation, not tests of IOI circuit faithfulness.

fits_no_version.finding: In GPT-2 Small, Position Swap and Name Swap patching at the residual sites selected from the IOI circuit puts most of the ΔLD effect in single NDM subspaces. Examples: h4 subspace 6 has effect 3.60 against 0.03 for the next subspace; h8 subspace 9 has 2.31 against 0.78. Gini values vary by test and normalization (0.38–0.90).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: IOI-circuit variables (previous token, S1 position, S name) at circuit-chosen residual sites in GPT-2 Small are largely localized in single unsupervised-learned subspaces.

record.problems: The paper reports averaged results over 1000 prompts without uncertainty estimates. The reported Gini metrics quantify concentration of patching effects, not the IOI behavior’s overall accuracy or the causal contribution of the 26-head circuit. The authors also note limitations in the subspace method, including imperfect partitions and hyperparameter sensitivity.
record.rows_left_out: Did not record identity, random, PCA, and SAE-feature baselines in Table 1 because they compare subspace-partition methods rather than test the IOI head circuit. Did not record test 5 because it concerns the Greater-than task. Did not record hyperparameter-sweep aggregate values in Tables 5–8 as circuit results; they concern NDM/SAE partition evaluation rather than the listed circuit claims.

untested.parts: All: the 26 heads, the 7 classes, and the faithfulness, completeness and minimality criteria.
All: no name-mover ablation and no backup-head analysis.
All: IOI is studied only in GPT-2 Small; Qwen and Gemma are tested on knowledge-conflict prompts.
All: no alternative circuit discovery is run on IOI.
All: no evaluation of the circuit's faithfulness or completeness under different ablations, metrics or prompt distributions.
All: name orders and templates are randomized but results are aggregated; there are no variant comparisons and no prompts with more names.

record.verdict_notes: The IOI circuit is assumed, not tested; the paper says the moved-information claims are backed by causal evidence from Wang et al. All Table 1 values compare partition methods, so they measure tool performance rather than the phenomenon. Hyperparameter and data-source sensitivity (Tables 5–7) concern NDM, not the circuit.

versions.untested_parts: The 26-head circuit, its seven classes and roles, and faithfulness, completeness, and minimality criteria.
Whether backup heads take over after main name-mover heads are ablated.
Whether the same circuit occurs in other models, sizes, checkpoints, or tasks. Other models are tested on knowledge-conflict prompts, not IOI.
Whether alternative circuit-finding methods, ablations, or metrics recover the IOI circuit.
Whether the circuit’s faithfulness or completeness depends on ablation type, metric, or prompt distribution, or whether it explains only part of IOI behavior.
Whether the same circuit carries IOI across prompt variants. The study aggregates random name orders and templates and does not test more-than-two-name prompts or circuit identity across variants.

rows.subject: GPT-2 Small
rows.operation_detail: Patch residual-stream subspace activations using Position Swap counterfactuals; report Gini coefficient over patching effects.

conditions.value: 1000 examples; name order uniformly random; templates randomly selected from a predefined list

rows.measure: Gini coefficient over subspace patching effects (raw ΔLD)
rows.baseline: 0 means effect evenly distributed across subspaces; 1 indicates maximal concentration
rows.note: Reports concentration of a circuit-related target-information effect, not whether the named attention heads perform their claimed roles.
rows.check: Gini of NDM subspace patching effects: a performance score for the study's own method, compared against baselines in Table 1. It is not a measure of the IOI circuit. It arguably should not be a circuit-result row.

rows.baseline: 0 means effect evenly distributed across subspaces; 1 indicates maximal concentration

rows.check: Same as r1 (dimension-normalized Gini); a method-performance value, not a circuit measurement.
